question: How does the paper from which Raffray's cited Brayton cycle method takes its efficiency expressions, S. Malang, H. Schnauder, M. S. Tillack, Combination of a self-cooled liquid metal breeder blanket with a gas turbine power conversion system, Fusion Engineering and Design 39-40 (1998) 561-567, represent the delivery of blanket and divertor heat to the helium Brayton cycle: a single lumped heater or intermediate heat exchanger with a stated terminal or approach temperature difference, or per-loop exchangers with their own duties and temperature spans; what cycle inlet and outlet temperatures and what heat-exchanger temperature difference does it use; and does that representation bear on the inconsistency among the published ARIES-CS branch duties and temperature spans and the published 707 C cycle outlet (Raffray et al. 2008, Table II, Table III, Fig. 12)?
where_to_look: ScienceDirect Fusion Engineering and Design volume 39-40, 1998, pages 561-567, Malang Schnauder Tillack self-cooled liquid metal breeder blanket gas turbine
UCSD ARIES program report library mirrors (qedfusion.org LIB REPORT, cer.ucsd.edu) for the ISFNT-4 1997 or ARIES-RS power conversion papers by Malang, Schnauder, Tillack
Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe (KIT) publication repository and OSTI.gov for the 1997-1998 report version
